question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution does the High Court exercise its original jurisdiction by issuing writs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 226 of the Indian Constitution empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and other legal rights.
 
• The writ jurisdiction includes issuing writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.
 
• Unlike Article 32 (Supreme Court), Article 226 covers not only fundamental rights but also other rights established by law.
 
• The High Court's writ jurisdiction extends to persons, authorities, and governments within its territorial limits.
 
• Article 226 serves as a vital mechanism for judicial review and upholding the rule of law in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writs in India:**

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** Protects against unlawful detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** Directs authorities to fulfill their duties.
 
• **Prohibition:** Prevents lower courts from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** Transfers cases to higher courts for review.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** Challenges the legality of a person's public office holding.
 
 
 
• **Article 32 vs Article 226:**
 
 
• Article 32 is limited to enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• Article 226 includes fundamental rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Territorial Jurisdiction:** High Courts can exercise writ jurisdiction over entities within their geographical boundaries.
 
• **Judicial Review:** Article 226 plays a crucial role in ensuring the accountability of public authorities and safeguarding individual rights.
 
• **Importance:** Article 226 is considered broader in scope than Article 32 and is essential for maintaining constitutional governance.
